rounds.restatement: When the math tokenizer meets a character it cannot place (a quote, backslash, non-ASCII letter, etc.) it must stop with an error instead of looping forever, so that resolveTemplate throws a TemplateError and render returns promptly with ok false and a located diagnostic, while every valid math expression keeps exactly the value it had before. Only core/src/expressions.ts may change.

findings.title: Unknown-character error is thrown as plain TypeError, so the interpreter discards it: strict mode reports a misleading missing-variable diagnostic and lenient mode renders ok with no diagnostic

serves.scenario: Interpreter.visitVariable swallows math errors and only re-surfaces them when they are MathSyntaxError (interpreter.ts:190-193). The new throw uses TypeError, so for ${{ 1 + "x" }} strict render reports code missing-variable, message "Variable '1 + \"x\"' not found" (the unknown-character message never reaches the user), and render(t, {}, {strictMode:false}) returns ok:true, output "", diagnostics [] - no diagnostic at all, contrary to c1 'returns promptly with a diagnostic' and the cycle goal 'ends the render with a located error'. The hang is fixed; the diagnostic is not.

findings.rubric: each criterion is met by the diff and its test (c1: returns promptly with a diagnostic)
findings.reproduction: In the worktree, transpile-require core/src and run render('${{ 1 + "x" }}', {}) -> diagnostics[0] = {code:'missing-variable', message:"Variable '1 + \"x\"' not found"}; then render('${{ 1 + "x" }}', {}, {strictMode:false}) -> {ok:true, output:'', diagnostics:[]}. Same for '${{ 1 + é }}'. Smallest fix: throw MathSyntaxError (already defined in errors.ts:90 and used for 'Unmatched parentheses' at expressions.ts:723) instead of TypeError at expressions.ts:689, so the interpreter surfaces the unknown-character message in strict mode (lenient-mode masking via MissingVariableError path should then be checked as well).
